fatal_blockers: Proposal 1 is already falsified by the hostile collision-shell evidence: all-eight and odd-holonomy have illegal mixed words whose quadratic walk features cancel completely. Any linear BCH/expander encoding E preserves zero, and the proposed [7,4,3] encoding is also underspecified for more than four collision coordinates.

Proposal 2 does not specify a linear syndrome or lattice realization of its nonlinear Gray/Lee map and alphabet shield. The fixed-degree shield a↦(a,a(a−1)) is covered by the polynomial finite-difference and integer-repair obstructions, while q≤3 over Z8 cannot discriminate the required logarithmic carry tower asymptotically.

Proposal 3 supplies neither a precommitted automaton family nor a polynomial bound on its width, family size, and binary output rank. Greedily selecting automata on the hostile suite is test-set overfitting, and 'every two-state automaton' is not a feasible or fully specified search when each input coordinate needs transition matrices.

Proposal 4's minors are quadratic signatures, so mandatory Boolean cubes produce exact finite-difference relations; taking the affine span of nonlinear lifts preserves rather than removes those superpositions. Moreover, rank-one matrices span the entire matrix space, so no linear zero-baseline shell can vanish on all legal rank-one words while charging every illegal combination.

Proposal 5 lacks the essential classifier: arbitrary elliptic-curve labels do not make all perfect-matching sums lie on one designated cheap translate while excluding odd covers. Kummer coordinates do not linearize group addition, so implementation requires an exponential sum dictionary or a bounded-fan-in addition tableau already blocked by the obstruction map.

Proposal 6 assumes without justification that YES has an isolating seed while every NO fiber is dense for every seed; lossless condensation does not imply this asymmetric fiber statement. Its bilinear seed coupling has cube trades, and the proposed idempotent selector repeats the already-falsified global-branch splice unless a genuinely new non-affine global matrix is specified.

Proposal 7 communicates through selected pair coordinates and endpoint incidence projections, which are proper marginals and remain vulnerable to rectangle kernels and odd holonomy. No additional global constraint, deterministic selector construction, all-mixed-word lower bound, or improved output-rank exponent is supplied; enumerating all regular selectors is also not a realistically bounded smallest experiment.

None of the seven proposals gives the currently required explicit polynomial-time matrix for arbitrary 3DM, a uniform sparse YES bound, a polynomially larger NO bound over every mixed word, and output-rank accounting. Their suggested finite tests could only recheck known obstruction instances or tune an unspecified family, so no proposed experiment is genuinely discriminating as written.
evidence: The Schur-walk verifier found all-eight illegal cost 6 and holonomy illegal cost 9 with every walk feature canceled. This directly defeats Proposal 1's quadratic collision vector and any linear post-encoding of it.

The proved bounded-signature theorem gives alternating cube relations for every fixed-degree polynomial signature, surviving linear rows, modular reduction, tensoring, and dense postprocessing. It applies directly to Proposals 1, 2's fixed-degree shield, 4, and 6's bilinear coupling whenever their stated cubes survive.

The tested global branch selector admitted a weight-9 rectangle splice, while global pair-feature and sparse-hash shells reduced the gap to at most 7/6 or worse. These are direct warnings against Proposals 6 and 7, not asymptotic theorems beyond the tested models.

Prior noncommutative and dense folds over M3(F4), F8, and A4 all failed exact mixed-word tests through pointed kernels or YES-baseline inflation. This does not rule out Proposal 3 universally, but it leaves its unsupported automaton-to-Hamming mechanism without positive verifier evidence.

The determinant/exterior dictionary tests retained short virtual states even after every compound state was added, while explicit dictionaries were exponential. This supports the stated affine-span and baseline blockers for Proposals 4 and 5.
All supplied positive tensor and integer results still terminate at the rank-compression wall; none of these proposals provides the missing asymmetric operation or sparse global classifier.
pro_reviews_fable.next_experiment: No implementation is authorized for these proposals as written. Revival requires a distinct mutation with a fully explicit arbitrary-instance matrix and precommitted bounded parameters; only then should one exact experiment enumerate every mixed word on held-out YES/NO, affine-closure, all-eight, and odd-holonomy instances while reporting worst-YES, best-NO, pointed kernels, and exact output rank.

fatal_blockers: Proposal 1 does not specify an exact cloud replacement, lifted affine fiber, or binary generator matrix. If cloud copies equal the original variable, its many paths are repeated Boolean functions subject to O1 cancellation; if copies are independent, new sheet-splicing and completeness obligations arise under O3, while existing all-eight and holonomy words already cancel every I27 walk feature.

Proposal 2 repeats the unresolved O7 rank-to-Hamming leap already falsified by dense two-sided condensers. Flattening rank is nonlinear, while outputting condensed matrix entries is linear but rank one does not imply sparse Hamming support; the condenser family and row encoders are also not uniquely specified.

Proposal 3 supplies no binary syndrome matrix or definition of its Fox-derivative rows. A fixed six-sheet S3 lift cannot create logarithmic systole over constant short base cycles, and collision forests have trivial monodromy, so O3 remains; any edge-interface linearization also risks O2, while universal completeness under the graph-dependent voltages is unproved under O4.

Proposal 4 has the wrong baseline and size accounting. A legal q-triple matching contributes up to sum_{k<=r} binom(q,k) standard monomials, which is q^{Theta(log q)} for r=Theta(log q), while conflict monomials can delete rather than expose illegal terms; fixed truncations remain vulnerable to O1 and the incidence binomials are unspecified.

Proposal 5 is directly blocked by O2 and O5: a signed 2x2x2 parity-cube perturbation has all three pair projections zero. Adding it to a matching leaves every P, G, and G^k unchanged, so all Gram features vanish while the original coefficient norm changes only additively; fixed primes cannot recover information absent from the projections.

Proposal 6 has no polynomial-time rule for Q: its SDP requires enumerating matchings and signed exact fibers, thereby using the source decision information. On Az=1 the A^T A term is constant, PSD triangle inequalities cap short affine trades by a constant multiple of the completeness radius, and this direct integer metric is not the O8 binary-syndrome transfer claimed.

None of the six proposals supplies polynomial output, worst-YES support, exact rank, and every-mixed-word soundness simultaneously. O6 is not directly triggered because these are not complete-assignment dictionaries, but avoiding O6 does not repair their O1-O5, O7, and O8 failures.
evidence: I27's exact finite test found ratio 11 on the ordinary suite, but all-eight and twisted holonomy contain illegal mixed words of costs 6 and 9 with zero walk charge. No bounded-degree source reduction, logarithmic-path soundness lemma, or polynomial rank theorem was obtained.

The frozen F8 multi-block condenser had worst YES 31 versus best NO 6 despite no pointed kernels. This verifies the relevant rank-versus-Hamming-support failure on every enumerated mixed word, though it is not a universal no-go theorem.

The obstruction map proves that every proper marginal kills the full parity cube. Pair-projection Gram powers are functions only of such marginals and therefore cannot distinguish their exact integer kernel.

Variable pair-projection CVP was already tested and achieved only squared norm 12 versus 14; direct integer incidence gives q versus q+2. These are additive finite gaps, not evidence for polynomial separation.
Exact syndrome-to-CVP transfer applies only after an explicit binary H,t with a proved syndrome-distance gap is supplied. None of these proposals reaches that prerequisite.
fable_reviews_pro.next_experiment: None for the proposals as written. Reopen only Proposal 1 after specifying an explicit polynomial-time cloud map and binary lift, proving legal completeness and nonduplicate path functions; then precommit one tiny cloud and enumerate every mixed word on all-eight, holonomy, affine-closure, and the 10/200 suite, rejecting unless hostile distance exceeds worst YES and the exact-rank exponent improves.
